channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Growing share of sellers in Brussels offloading apartments that need renovation work
item.description: Brussels' energy performance rules are pushing many homeowners to sell properties that need renovation, even if it means a lower price.

item.title: Former Schaerbeek city councillor De Herde to appear in court on suspicion of rape
item.description: Former Schaerbeek city councillor Michel De Herde (ex-DéFI), suspected of raping several victims, is due to appear in court in March 2027.

item.title: New data centre in Brussels to account for 3% of region’s total electricity consumption
item.description: "Every Megawatt of grid capacity allocated to these servers is capacity that can no longer be used for a hospital, a tram depot, or an electric vehicle charging station."

item.title: Belgian fixed term energy contracts have climbed €1,400 since March
item.description: In Brussels, the average unit price for gas has more than doubled, moving from 5.47 c€/kWh in March to 11.47 c€/kWh now.

item.title: 'I have HIV. Now what do I do?' A Brussels man on life after diagnosis
item.description: Diagnosed with HIV at 22, Maël Gerday speaks about stigma, rejection, relationships and learning to live openly with the virus.

item.title: Explosion damages Brussels building overnight
item.description: Several windows were blown out by the explosion but no one was injured.

item.title: Group of young people harass train attendant near Brussels
item.description: The group had already caused disruption on another train in Leuven before the incident.

item.title: About 100 people gather in Brussels to commemorate Novi Sad disaster
item.description: Two years ago, a station railway canopy collapsed and killed 16 people in Serbia, sparking a widespread anti-government movement.

item.title: Heavy equipment deployed to extinguish raging Brussels fire
item.description: The last remaining hotspot of the fire is not accessible as the building's structure has been severely damaged.

item.title: Brussels CPAS offices criticise lack of consultation on benefit system
item.description: Under the federal circular, social benefits are now heavily linked to a recipient's willingness to work.

item.title: Severe fire in Brussels building
item.description: One person suffered severe smoke inhalation.

item.title: 'Diversity within diversity': Over 80% of couples in Brussels are bicultural
item.description: While every relationship has its challenges, having different mother tongues, family traditions or cultural expectations can make love even harder to navigate.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 30 October - 1 November
item.description: Whether you're in the mood to celebrate the spooky season or not, there's something for everyone to enjoy in Brussels this weekend.

item.title: City of Brussels loses millions as it temporarily extends casino license
item.description: The City of Brussels will lose just under €3 million in revenue as it had to temporarily extend the exploitation license for the Grand Casino.

item.title: One in 16 teaching hours left without a teacher in Flemish secondary schools
item.description: Nearly 6% of teaching hours in Flemish secondary schools went uncovered in March 2025, according to a new report by the Belgian Court of Audit.

item.title: Brussels police investigates potential child kidnapping in Anderlecht street
item.description: Two masked persons reportedly stepped out of a vehicle and forced a child to get in the van.

item.title: Brussels fire extinguisher manufacturer leaves behind massive PFAS contamination as bankruptcy threatens clean-up
item.description: A former fire extinguisher manufacturer in Uccle has left behind severe PFAS contamination, with clean-up costs expected to run into millions of euros.

item.title: Young lawyer stabbed to death in Brussels apartment, ex-partner arrested
item.description: A young legal professional was found stabbed to death in her apartment in Auderghem, during the night of 24 to 25 October. Her former partner has reportedly been arrested and charged with murder.

item.title: The trouble with Belgium: In Brussels, 'good enough' is good enough
item.description: Work here is not character-defining but adjacent to one’s identity: we can do things quickly, and then enjoy life. Or even the other way around.

item.title: ‘Every day, we send people back onto the street’: Brussels struggles with rising crack addiction
item.description: “There has been no inflation on cocaine for many years. That gram you paid €50 for ten years ago still costs €50.”
